fields.description:
## The defect

`scripts/check_config_reads.py` (the 6754 gate, wired at `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:476`)
is meant to fail CI when a `_config_schema.py` dataclass field has no read site unless it carries
a `# read-via:` marker. It does not do that.

`_collect_reads` (script lines ~84-101) builds a GLOBAL SET of attribute NAMES read anywhere under
`src/rebar`, then the check is effectively `field_name in reads` -- NOT `Class.field`.

So any field whose bare name is read on ANY other object anywhere in the tree passes the gate,
regardless of whether that field itself is ever read.

## Confirmed instance

`CodeHealthConfig.enabled` (`src/rebar/_config_schema.py`) has ZERO read sites -- nothing gates on
it, and structural metrics run even at the default `enabled=False`. It nevertheless passes the gate
and carries no `# read-via:` marker, because `.enabled` is read elsewhere (`ui.enabled`,
`LangfuseConfig`, and under `llm/`).

Contrast the since-removed `CodeHealthConfig.analyzers`, whose bare name was read NOWHERE in the
tree, so it DID trip the gate and needed the marker `# read-via: inert pending bug
dce2-b93d-4112-451c` to keep CI green.

That asymmetry is the tell: the gate catches an inert field only when its name happens to be
globally unique. That is luck, not a check.

## Why this matters beyond one field

This is a FALSE-NEGATIVE class, not a single miss. Common field names -- `enabled`, `path`,
`timeout`, `remote`, `branch`, `mode` -- are exactly the ones most likely to be reused across
configs and therefore exactly the ones this gate cannot police. The inert-config family it exists
to prevent (281f, 9d7a, dce2) is precisely the family it will keep missing.

## SCOPE (operator ruling, 2026-08-05) -- fix the gate, REPORT what it flags, do NOT triage

The operator has ruled on scope for this ticket. It is recorded here in the description (not only
in a comment) because the plan reviewer reads the description:

**In scope.** Fix the name-resolution defect so a read is resolved to its OWNING dataclass rather
than matched as a bare attribute name anywhere under `src/rebar`. Then run the fixed gate across
the whole schema and REPORT the newly-flagged fields.

**Explicitly OUT of scope: triaging the newly-flagged fields.** Each newly-flagged field is a
wire-it-or-delete-it PRODUCT judgement -- the same call the operator made individually for
`dce2-b93d-4112-451c` (delete) and `a573-00ea-2bf6-4eb1` (delete). Rationale: an agent must not make
those calls unsupervised inside a gate fix. Deleting or wiring a config field changes user-visible
behaviour and is a decision that belongs to the operator, not to a side effect of a checker
correction. So this ticket reports the list and stops; each entry is dispositioned separately.

**Sequencing (the practical consequence).** The fixed gate will fail CI on the fields it newly
flags, so the fix cannot land bare. The operator sanctioned two mechanisms: (a) land the fix with
accurate `# read-via:` markers -- factual pointers for fields that ARE read through indirection, and
a tracking-ticket pointer for a field that is genuinely inert -- which is the mechanism the codebase
already uses (`TrackerConfig.branch`, `ReconcilerConfig.lock_lease_secs`, the removed
`CodeHealthConfig.analyzers`); or (b) land the fix behind resolution of those fields.

**THIS TICKET CHOOSES (a).** Reason: (b) blocks a correct checker behind product decisions that are
not this ticket's to make, and leaves the false-negative class live in the meantime. Under (a) each
marker must be ACCURATE -- it either cites the real reader, or names a real open tracking ticket.
Silently exempting a field to make CI green is forbidden.

**Known already-ruled instance.** `CodeHealthConfig.enabled` is being REMOVED under bug
`a573-00ea-2bf6-4eb1` (Gerrit change 1422, still open at the time of writing). It is therefore
reported separately rather than double-triaged; its marker names a573 as the tracking ticket and
sits on the field's own line so a573's deletion of that line removes the marker with it.

## Required negative fixtures (the gate must NOT false-fire on these)

A correct owning-dataclass resolver still has to tolerate legitimate STRING-keyed reads. A prior
manual sweep of all config dataclass fields (under a573) found these live-but-string-read cases;
they are required negative fixtures for the fixed gate:

- `ReconcilerConfig.lock_lease_secs` -- read via `getattr` in
  `_engine/rebar_reconciler/_advisory_lock.py`; already carries a `# read-via:` marker.
- `VerifyConfig.require_plan_review_for_close` (and its `require_plan_review_for_claim` /
  `require_completion_verification_for_close` siblings) -- read via
  `gate_enabled(root, "<key>", ...)` string keys in `_commands/gates.py`; already carry markers.

The fixed gate must leave these passing.

## Design of the fix

Replace the global name set with a per-read owner resolution:

1. Parse `_config_schema.py` into `class -> {field -> annotation}`, and derive the SECTION map from
   the root `Config` dataclass (`code_health -> CodeHealthConfig`, etc.).
2. For every `*.py` under `src/rebar` (minus the existing `_config_schema.py` / `config.py` plumbing
   exclusion), resolve the RECEIVER expression of each `ast.Attribute` read to a set of candidate
   owning schema classes, using: the section-attribute name (`x.code_health` -> `CodeHealthConfig`),
   parameter/variable annotations naming a schema class, local assignment propagation
   (`m = cfg.mcp; m.readonly`), function RETURN annotations (`load_config() -> Config`), `IfExp` /
   `BoolOp` branches, and a cross-module fixed point that binds unannotated PARAMETERS from their
   call sites (`build_composite_verifier(mcp_cfg)` called with `cfg.mcp`).
3. A field is satisfied only by a read whose resolved owner set contains its declaring class.

Unresolvable receivers contribute nothing, so the resolver stays fail-QUIET in the one direction
that cannot break CI on a live field: an ambiguity suppresses a firing rather than inventing one.
Function names are keyed bare (module-agnostic), which can only widen a binding -- again fail-quiet.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The gate resolves a read to the OWNING dataclass, not a bare attribute name -- a field is
      satisfied only by a read of that class's instance, so a same-named attribute on an unrelated
      config no longer satisfies it.
- [ ] A RED-first test proves the CURRENT gate passes a synthetic inert field whose name is reused
      elsewhere, and that the fixed gate fails it. (Run both versions in-process from a snapshot
      copy of the pre-fix script -- never `git stash`, which is global across worktrees on this
      host.)
- [ ] The two required negative fixtures above are pinned as tests and still pass.
- [ ] The gate is re-run across the whole existing `_config_schema.py` and every newly-flagged field
      is REPORTED (in a ticket comment and in the change description). Per the operator ruling above
      they are NOT triaged here.
- [ ] Each newly-flagged field gets an ACCURATE `# read-via:` marker -- citing its real reader where
      one exists, or naming a real open tracking ticket where it does not -- so the fix lands
      CI-green without a silent exemption.
- [ ] `CodeHealthConfig.enabled` is reported against `a573-00ea-2bf6-4eb1` rather than
      re-triaged here.
- [ ] Any field whose marker points at a CLOSED ticket is reported rather than silently accepted.

## Provenance

Found by a code-trace archaeology pass over the metrics/code-health system while scoping
dce2-b93d-4112-451c. The gate's own escape hatch for `analyzers` was self-referential -- the bug id
in the marker is what kept CI green -- which is legitimate, but it masked that the gate could not
have caught the neighbouring field at all.
